newsitem.title: India: North India hit by third earthquake in 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: North India hit by third earthquake in 24 hours.

text.p: A moderate earthquake, the third in 48 hours in western and northern India, shook the summer capital of India's northern Jammu and Kashmir state on Tuesday, officials said.
Residents reported feeling tremors, but police and state authorities said there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
Two tremors struck Srinagar the first at 5.15 p.m. (1145 GMT) for 52 seconds and the second at 5.16 (1146 GMT) for 40 seconds, the officials said.
Officials at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) could not immediately be contacted for precise details of the epicentre or magnitude of the latest earthquake.
Earlier on Tuesday, an earthquake measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale, struck the northeastern state of Assam at 5:42 a.m. (0012 GMT).
Its epicentre was in Cachar district, about 300 km (180 miles) southwest of the state capital Guwahati, the IMD said.
Late on Sunday, an earthquake also measuring 4.8 on the Richter scale struck the western state of Gujarat.
In 1993, a quake of 6.4 on the Richter scale devastated a large area of neighbouring Maharashtra state, killing more than 11,000 people, and leaving about 150,000 homeless.
Earthquakes between four and five on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
